title: Imran Khan’s Health, Iran Under Sanctions
author: Drop Site News
content:
Pakistan's imprisoned former prime minister Imran Khan was recently taken from
prison to hospital for medical treatment amid reports of his failing health in
custody, including continued loss of eyesight in his right eye. The fate of
Khan, the country's most popular politician, has held politics in limbo in the
nuclear-armed country of 240 million for the past three years. While the
ruling military junta has expanded its ties with Washington, and begun
building new alliances with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, domestic political and
economic conditions continue to deteriorate within Pakistan itself--including
brutal military crackdowns on protests in the province of Kashmir,
insurgencies in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and rampaging inflation
nationwide triggered in part by the ongoing Iran War.

On this week's episode of the Drop Site News livestream, host**Murtaza
Hussain** discusses the fate of Khan and the future of Pakistan with Drop Site
reporter **Waqas Ahmed**.

Later in the episode, Murtaza is joined by **Esfandyar Batmanghelidj** , head
of the Bourse and Bazaar Foundation economic think tank to discuss the status
of the Iran War, including the dueling blockades over the Strait of Hormuz and
economic impact of U.S. sanctions on civilians in Iran. Batmanghelidj also
provides a prognosis on the future of the conflict, which has shifted to an
economic siege amid the U.S. Treasury declaration of an "Economic D-Day"
against Iran this week, while giving an analysis of whether these measures
will lead to compromise or escalation in the current standoff.
